How close arms submitted and revised come to the 2011 targets

The model/target ratio of every calibration target at t = 100, for both arms and both regions; how the 28 September search for revised moved its instruments and ratios; whether revised’s consumption is half of submitted’s (it is not); and why the EU central bank holds no RoW bills while advances are negative.

Author

LEEDS_MODEL — JUST2CE

Published

September 29, 2026

Written: 2026-09-29 · Repo at: main @ 8e07250, plus the uncommitted R/plot_calibration_ratios.R and its outputs. Reads: the cached 100-period baselines output/scenarios/arms/{submitted,revised,adjudicated}/runs/baseline.RDS (cut 2026-09-23, 2026-09-29 07:35 and 2026-09-29 06:52), through the committed tables output/calibration/calibration_ratio_cells_20260929.csv, consumption_levels_20260929.csv and advances_revised_20260929.csv, which Rscript R/plot_calibration_ratios.R writes.

Which revised this describes. The calibrated baseline of 28 September, cut 2026-09-29 07:35, before the same day’s restart fix (the money wage is now carried across the spin-up) and change R10. That run is kept as output/scenarios/arms/revised/runs/baseline_pre_wagecarry_20260929.RDS. The cached revised baseline is now the fixed but uncalibrated one; see qmd/reports/2026-09-29-equation-audit.qmd §2 for how its ratios moved.

Summary

  • The targets. data/target_values.xlsx holds twelve 2011 magnitudes per region (EU = Z1, RoW = Z2). Every ratio below is the model value at t = 100 divided by its target, in the model’s unit of 10 bn EUR.
    • The three nominal concepts are value added, the deficit and the debt stock. They are divided first by the region’s consumption deflator pa, indexed so that t = 2 = 1. This is calib_fitness(deflate = TRUE), the convention every calibration search has used.
  • revised fits better overall. The objective the searches minimised (scale = "gdp", mean squared miss in units of GDP) is 0.00082 for revised against 0.01937 for submitted.
    • revised puts value added, the debt stock, debt/VA and the deficit on target in both regions.
    • submitted overshoots value added by 14–16% and the debt stock by 24% (EU) and 60% (RoW).
  • revised fits worse on three things:
    • RoW real investment, 0.75 of target;
    • trade in both directions, 0.87–0.89 of target;
    • RoW gross output, 0.95.
  • Consumption is not half. At t = 100 revised’s real consumption is 3.1% above submitted’s in the EU and 3.1% below it in RoW, and both are within 5.5% of target.
    • The impression came from the arm report output/html/reports/arms/revised.html, which plots each series indexed to its own value at t = 2.
    • The fixed-price arms start at t = 2 from a seed at about 43% of target and grow 2.4-fold. revised starts near its calibrated level and settles 9% lower.
    • Indexed, therefore, revised looks like about 0.38 of the other arm. That is a picture of two starting points, not of two consumption levels.
  • b_cb_s_Z2 = 0 is a design choice; negative advances are a sign convention.
    • Change R6 freezes the EU central bank’s RoW-bill stock at its t = 1 value, which is 0.
    • Change R7 defines a negative A_d as the banks’ reserve deposit at the central bank. Both balance sheets and the gold-flow identity read the sign consistently.
  • Not a bug, but a defect: the banks make persistent losses. The EU banks hold 959.3 of their 1,626.8 of deposits (59%) as reserves that earn nothing. RoW banks hold 49% that way.
    • Both pay a deposit rate above the bill rate.
    • Bank profit f_b is therefore negative in every period: -17.1 (EU) and -47.3 (RoW) at t = 100.

Reading the table.

  • Exports and imports mirror each other by construction. In a two-region model EU real exports are RoW real final imports, which is why the pairs 0.887 / 0.887 and 0.871 / 0.871 repeat across the two regions.
  • The trade shortfall. In revised, trade is 11–13% below its 2011 level in both directions. Two causes are candidates, and neither is separated yet:
    • the Armington gap (hand-off item 2, defect 2);
    • the restart price jump (item 2, defect 3), which leaves Armington reference prices away from the stationary prices.
  • RoW investment at 0.75. This is a property of revised’s capital block (R4, R9: investment is replacement demand K·x plus accumulation). The 09-28 calibration log recorded it as unfixed. The data’s RoW net investment is 203 per period, so the model misses the gross level, not the net one.

Figure B — the search that calibrated revised

What the figure shows, stage by stage. revised was calibrated in three stages, and Figure B covers the middle one.

  1. Route A: the current account. R/calibrate_revised_cab.R set the EU share of household wealth in RoW equity (Z1_lambdaE0_2, 0.02 in the workbook, not estimated) so that the EU current account is zero. This is what makes the baseline stationary.
    • Output: output/calibration/revised_cab_search_2026092{8,9}.csv, 8 + 4 runs. They are not plotted, because they are one-dimensional.
    • Result: 0.03714.
  2. The joint search (Figure B), 18 runs.
    • Instruments:
      • a scale on the EU and RoW tax rates θ_w and θ_c, which sets the level of activity (with a balanced budget, VA = (G + public investment + interest) / net tax rate);
      • the same equity share, re-tuned jointly with the scale.
    • Adopted: run 16, with scales 0.7424 (EU) and 0.5565 (RoW) and share 0.03227. From the 29 September commit 442f5f2 these are the workbook’s base values, so a scale of 1 is now the calibrated state.
    • Debt was not calibrated in this stage. The debt endowment was 0 throughout, so debt/VA wandered: at run 16 it was −0.55 in the EU and 2.13 in RoW, ratios −0.67 and 2.5.
  3. The debt endowment. R/calibrate_revised_debt.R issued bills to each region’s own central bank at t = 1 of the spin-up: 1466.4 (EU) and −5045.7 (RoW).
    • Why the instrument is an initial condition: under R6 debt and gold share a unit root once the current account is zero, so no flow parameter pins the debt level.
    • Measured on 09-28: the endowment moves debt one for one and leaves value added, consumption and gross output identical to four digits.
    • Figure B confirms it: the ‘cal’ points for the four activity concepts sit exactly on run 16, and debt/VA and the debt stock jump to 1.

What the search did not record. Real exports, final imports, intermediate imports, final demand, government spending and the deficit are not in the search file, so their evolution cannot be plotted without re-running the 18 configurations. The recorded levels are also undeflated: pa is not in the file. The final ratios of all twelve concepts are in Figure A.

Is revised’s consumption half of submitted’s?

No. The variable is Z*_c, “Total Real Consumption”, in 10 bn EUR at base prices (data/Variable_Definitions.csv). Nominal consumption is pa × c.

Real consumption, its own index from t = 2, the consumption deflator and nominal consumption. adjudicated is the reference arm the per-arm reports plot revised against.
arm region c at t = 2 c at t = 100 c(100) / c(2) pa at t = 100 nominal pa·c at t = 100 2011 target C
adjudicated EU 270.9 650.5 2.401 1.070 696.2 626.3
adjudicated RoW 971.7 2498.4 2.571 1.067 2666.1 2370.7
submitted EU 270.4 641.0 2.370 1.070 686.0 626.3
submitted RoW 971.1 2488.6 2.563 1.067 2655.6 2370.7
revised EU 725.7 660.6 0.910 1.089 719.3 626.3
revised RoW 2548.2 2412.1 0.947 1.188 2865.1 2370.7
  • In volume at t = 100:
    • EU: revised 660.6 against submitted 641.0, +3.1%;
    • RoW: 2,412.1 against 2,488.6, -3.1%.
  • In money: revised is higher in both regions, because its deflator is higher.
    • pa is 1.089 (EU) and 1.188 (RoW) against 1.070 and 1.067.
    • The reason is that R1 measures prices of production in money units.
  • So a price-level difference does not hide a volume difference here. Both arms deflate c the same way, and their volumes differ by 3%.
  • Where “half” came from. The arm report (qmd/reports/arms/arm-baseline.qmd, rendered as output/html/reports/arms/revised.html) plots revised against adjudicated, with every series divided by its own value at t = 2.
    • adjudicated’s EU consumption runs from 270.9 to 650.5, an index of 2.40, because the fixed-price arms start from the old seed at 43% of target.
    • revised’s starts at 725.7 and ends at 660.6, an index of 0.91.
    • On that panel revised therefore sits at 0.91 / 2.40 = 0.38 of adjudicated.
  • Why revised starts high. Its t = 2 value is itself the restart overshoot: c is 701.4 at t = 1, 725.7 at t = 2 and 659.3 at t = 3. That is the same period as the 6–18% price jump at the spin-up restart (hand-off item 2, defect 3). So the index base is the worst possible period for this arm.
  • Recommendation. The arm reports should plot levels, or index to the target, whenever the two arms start from different initial states. Not changed here; a one-line option in arm-baseline.qmd.

Why is b_cb_s_Z2 0 while advances are negative?

The two facts are unrelated.

Z1_b_cb_s_Z2 is the EU central bank’s stock of RoW bills. It is 0 in every period because R6 (G&L OPENFIX) freezes it at its previous value (model/code/MVP_model_2026.R:1947, sim['Z1_b_cb_s_Z2', i] <- sim['Z1_b_cb_s_Z2', i - 1]), and its t = 1 value is 0.

  • The freeze is deliberate. It cuts the RoW treasury → EU central bank → EU treasury interest circuit that compounded at 1 + r_b in the older arms (engine comment at lines 1935–1946).
  • The workbook’s b_cb_d_Z2 is among the 27 labels revised never reads (output/calibration/workbook_usage_revised_20260929.csv).
  • Under OPENFIX the balance of payments settles in gold or, not in this stock. That is the closure’s defining choice.

a_d is the banks’ demand for central-bank advances. Under R7 (MVP_model_2026.R:683) banks demand bills as a fixed share of deposits, b_b = bank_bill_ratio × M_s (0.1 in both regions), and advances clear the bank balance sheet:

\[A_d = L_s + B_b - M_s .\]

When deposits exceed loans plus bills, A_d is negative. The engine comment at line 187 states the convention: “negative = reserve deposits at the CB”.

The sign is used consistently everywhere it appears. Checked:

  • Bank balance sheet. Assets L + B_b, liabilities M + A. A negative A is an asset of the banks.
  • Central-bank balance sheet. Supply a_s = a_d (line 857). The gold-flow identity (line 1957) subtracts Δa_s from ΔH. A fall in A, i.e. a rise in reserves, is therefore a CB liability that adds to its reserve assets, which is the right direction.
  • World gold conservation. run.model()’s consistency check measures it, and it closes (the 09-28 calibration recorded a consistency error of 4.3e-9).

What is a defect: those reserves earn nothing, and the banks lose money.

  • The balance sheet. At t = 100 the EU banks hold 1,626.8 of deposits against 504.8 of loans and 162.7 of bills, so 959.3 sits at the central bank.
  • Why they lose money. Bank profit (line 700) is \(f_b = r_l L_f + r_b B_b - r_m M_s + r_h L_h\). It has no term in A, so the reserves earn nothing.
    • The deposit rate rm is 0.0226, above the bill rate rb 0.0216.
    • f_b is therefore negative in every period: -17.1 (EU) and -47.3 (RoW).
  • This is consistent accounting of an implausible configuration. As recalled, not yet checked against the book: in G&L’s ch. 10 bank model reserves are a required fraction of deposits and bills are the residual asset, so banks never sit on 59% of their deposits as idle reserves.
  • Two candidate fixes, for a decision:
    1. calibrate bank_bill_ratio so that A_d ≈ 0, making bills rather than reserves the residual asset. That is roughly 0.69 (EU) and 0.59 (RoW) at the t = 100 balance sheets, since (M − L)/M = 0.69 / 0.59;
    2. pay the policy rate on reserves, adding ra × A to both f_b and f_cb.
  • Neither is made here. Either changes revised’s calibrated state and needs a re-cut.

Found in passing

  • CLAUDE.md is out of date on one fact. It says the gold endowment is “1,500 each, inert”. The workbook holds Z1_gold_endowment = 1,500 and Z2_gold_endowment = 2,500, raised on 09-28 because RoW gold ended at −586 (session log 2026-09-29 §6).
  • Search file headers. The joint-search file’s instrument columns are d1, d2, lambda, s1 and s2. d1 and d2 are the debt endowments, 0 in all 18 runs, and s1/s2 are the tax scales. The header does not say this; the script’s comment (R/calibrate_revised_debt.R:15) does.

Reproduce

Rscript R/plot_calibration_ratios.R    # figures + three CSVs, from the cached baselines (~10 s)
quarto render qmd/reports/2026-09-29-calibration-ratios.qmd --to html --output-dir ../../output/html/reports
